title: Swe senior scenario code review disagreement
topic: Swe senior scenario code review disagreement
question: A more junior engineer pushes back on your code review comment, they disagree with your suggested approach and defend their original implementation. How do you handle it?
idealAnswer:
Doesn't default to just overruling them on authority, engages with their specific reasoning and either finds it has a point or explains concretely why the concern doesn't hold up

Articulates the actual cost of not making the change in specific terms (maintainability, a pattern that will bite the team later, consistency with the rest of the codebase) rather than a vague appeal to 'best practice' or personal preference

Recognizes when a disagreement is a matter of genuine tradeoffs versus a hard correctness or safety issue, and calibrates how hard to push based on which one it is, not every review comment deserves the same level of insistence

Treats it as a mentoring moment as much as a code quality one, a strong answer cares about the junior engineer actually understanding the reasoning, not just complying

Shows a path forward if they still disagree after a good-faith discussion, e.g. deferring to them for this one if it's genuinely not high-stakes, or looping in a third opinion if it matters enough to resolve, rather than an unresolved standoff
